title: Ops + Finance Console usage reconciliation review
summary: Redwood walkthrough of per-route usage dashboards, reconciliation with FinOps, and a proposed pilot to validate per-route chargeback and KV cache savings. Customer concerned about SSO, audit logs, and cost attribution accuracy; asked for sample export and SLA/hosted vs dedicated guidance.
action_items: Alex Chen: Share per-route export CSV and mapping template by 2026-01-22
Priya Natarajan: Run a short inference latency/cost comparison for their 'triage-bot' route and send results by 2026-01-27
Liam O'Connor: Provide sample route tags and the current billing view from their cloud by 2026-01-25
next_steps: Redwood to provision 2-week pilot on a small set of routes (triage-bot, triage-embed)
Schedule security follow-up with Redwood security team (SSO/KMS deep dive)
Send contract/pricing templated for Dedicated vs Hosted options
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-20 15:00 UTC — Duration 45m
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Natarajan — Redwood; Liam O'Connor, Nina Patel, Sanjay Rao — Marigold Health

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros — I'm Alex in account, Priya's our solutions engineer. How are you folks doing?
[00:06] Liam: Yeah all good thanks. Excited to see the console pieces you mentioned. We're trying to get ops and finance on the same page for route-level costing.
[00:12] Nina: Hi all — Nina here, platform lead. Our ask: make it easy to reconcile reduct— reconcile usage against invoice and attribute to product teams.
[00:18] Sanjay: Sanjay from FinOps, and my big question is accuracy. If we charge teams based on route we need the numbers to match our cloud bill, or at least be explainable.
[00:25] Priya: Totally. We'll walk through the per-route dashboards and the CSV export. I'll show how route tags map to cost buckets and where small divergences can come from.

[00:40] Priya: (screen share) Ok starting at the Console home, you can see Overview, Models, Routes, and Usage. We built a per-route lens — this is 'Traffic by Route' which breaks down token count, latency p50/p95, and cost estimate per route. Note that cost estimate is derived from current model byte rate + GPU infer factors.
[01:05] Liam: That estimate, is it post-batching? Like if we do batching at the runtime level will the per-token cost change?
[01:10] Priya: Good question. The console's cost estimate toggles between 'raw per-token' and 'effective per-token' which factors batching and KV cache savings. There is a config that says whether to use observed batching efficiency for the last 24h vs recommended batching profile.
[01:28] Nina: Can we pin a model variant per route? We have a production route that needs stable latency and will accept slightly higher cost.
[01:34] Priya: Yep — route-level config supports model pinning and can attach rollout policies. So you can say route X uses model-7b-q4 for low-cost baseline and route X-prod pins to 13b-fp16 with a canary. The dashboard will reflect the chosen variant in cost calculations.

[02:02] Sanjay: Walk me through reconciliation differences. If your console says $1200 for a route for the month but our cloud bill shows GPU spend of $1150, how do we explain the $50 delta?
[02:12] Alex: A few common sources: (1) sampling windows — console may extrapolate from daily observed patterns, (2) differences in amortized infra like NIC costs, and (3) network or storage egress if your infra has it. We include a reconciliation tab that shows mapping to cloud line items and a probable-delta explanation.
[02:32] Priya: And we provide raw per-request export — tokens, model, route tag, timestamp — so you can join that with your billing export. We'll share a mapping template.

[02:50] Nina: How reliable are the timestamps? Our billing is per-hour, sometimes per-minute. We need to group to the same window.
[02:57] Priya: Timestamps are UTC with millisecond precision but the reconciliation tool aggregates to hourly or daily buckets to match whichever you prefer. You can choose the timezone and bucket size in the export UI.

[03:20] Liam: You mentioned KV cache. Our triage-bot uses long context often. How do you show cache hits affecting cost?
[03:26] Priya: We surface a 'KV hit rate' per route. For example, triage-bot shows 42% KV hit for the last week which reduces effective token regeneration. The 'effective tokens' field subtracts estimated regenerated tokens due to cache hits.
[03:40] Sanjay: Does that mean if KV hit rate improves after tuning, the cost numbers will drop retroactively?
[03:46] Priya: We won't rewrite history. The console shows observed vs estimated; historical rows will show the original observed tokens and a parallel field for 'estimated effective tokens'. So you can see the trend and project savings.

[04:10] Alex: A lot of customers find the per-route chargeback view useful — you can assign a route owner and an accounting code. Then we generate per-team rollups which you can export to your ledger.
[04:21] Nina: How do we handle shared models used by multiple routes? We want to avoid double charging model-level infra.
[04:26] Priya: We have an allocation algorithm. By default it's proportional to token usage per route across a time window. You can override with static allocation weights if you prefer to split infra evenly.

[04:48] Liam: Security stuff — SSO, audit logs, data retention. We need SOC2 evidence and a KMS integration.
[04:55] Alex: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Audit logs include request-level metadata and are exportable to your SIEM. For crypto, we integrate with KMS/HSM in Private deployments; for Hosted we have customer-managed key support planned in our roadmap — we'll capture that in the security follow-up.
[05:20] Sanjay: SLA question: if we move some routes to Dedicated to guarantee latency, how does pricing change and how is that reflected in the console?
[05:28] Priya: Console supports dedicated pool binding on a per-route basis. The cost model will then show a 'fixed reserved capacity amortization' line item plus the variable token cost. We can show both booked reservation amortization and usage delta. For short pilots we usually recommend burst-on-dedicated rather than full reservation.

[06:00] Nina: Can we label routes by product, team, and environment (prod/stage) and get the rollups by any of those dimensions?
[06:07] Priya: Yes — tags are first-class. You can filter dashboards, pivot by tag, and export grouped sums. We also auto-detect common tag mismatches and suggest harmonization rules.

[06:34] Alex: Quick demo of an example export: (shows CSV) you get columns route_id, route_name, tag_product, tag_team, model_variant, tokens_consumed, kv_hits, effective_tokens, latency_p50, cost_estimate_usd, timestamp_bucket. You can load this into your financial tool.
[07:02] Sanjay: Does the cost_estimate include network or just raw compute?
[07:06] Priya: It includes compute, memory amortization, and an optional network egress estimate if you enable that toggle. By default we leave network off unless you tell us your egress rates so we don't guess wrongly.

[07:30] Liam: On accuracy: we've seen other tools round tokenization differently which changes totals. How does Redwood tokenize, and is it consistent with billing?
[07:38] Priya: We use the model's tokenizer for count — same approach as model-level charge. Occasionally tokenizers differ by model family; we report the model used and tokenizer version in the export row so you can reconcile.

[08:05] Nina: About sampling — you mentioned console can extrapolate. For finance we need deterministic month-end numbers — can you run full capture?
[08:13] Priya: For pilots we can enable a full capture mode that writes every request detail to S3 for the period. That's more storage but gives you deterministic numbers. We'll do a short pilot with full capture for reconciliation testing.

[08:40] Sanjay: Is there a drift analysis? Like if our internal billing vs Redwood differs over time, does the console show trending deltas and likely causes?
[08:48] Priya: Yes — the reconciliation dashboard surfaces drift and correlates with config changes (model swaps, workload spikes). We also surface anomalies where tokenization or timestamp mismatches likely caused issues.

[09:10] Alex: Let's go through a concrete route — triage-bot. Priya, pull up triage-bot.
[09:16] Priya: (pulls up route) Triaged-bot — ok noted some transcription noise but you can see triage-bot has the following: 1.2M tokens for last 30d, avg latency 120ms p50, p95 320ms, KV hit 42%, cost estimate $1,250. Breakdown shows model cost $900, amortized infra $250, and small network if enabled.
[09:40] Liam: That $900 — is that for the specific model variant? Last month we ran a canary against higher-capacity model and saw an increase.
[09:46] Priya: Correct — and you can drill into the timeline to see cost per variant during the canary window. Also we show the canary's cost delta and an automatic rollback suggestion if drift exceeds your threshold.

[10:05] Sanjay: For chargeback, we need a GL code per route. Does Redwood let us set mapping and export to our ledger format?
[10:12] Alex: You can set GL code as a route attribute and we support export templates matching common ledger schemas. We'll add a sample for Marigold's chart of accounts in the action items.

[10:32] Nina: How do we forecast costs if we increase traffic by 3x for a product launch?
[10:37] Priya: There's a 'what-if' simulator. Input traffic multiplier, choose whether batching improves, and it projects cost and recommended changes like switching to a quantized variant or adding KV caching. It also flags performance risk.

[11:05] Liam: About private deployment — we have PHI concerns. If we go Private, do we still get the Console and the same dashboards?
[11:12] Alex: Yes. Console can be hosted either by Redwood with VPC peering or as a customer-managed control plane in your environment (on-prem). All dashboard features are identical; the only difference is where the control plane and audit logs live.

[11:36] Sanjay: For KMS and encryption at rest, what's supported on hosted?
[11:40] Priya: On Hosted we currently encrypt at rest and in transit with Redwood-managed keys; customer-managed KMS is available for Private and coming to Hosted as an opt-in beta (we'll add you to the waitlist if you want).

[12:00] Nina: Any hooks for our internal chargeback system — webhooks or SFTP?
[12:05] Priya: We support SFTP drops, S3 export, and webhook pushes. For higher assurance we can also do direct push to a customer-owned ingestion endpoint.

[12:30] (15 minute mark) Speaker 1: There's a little cross talk.
[12:35] Alex: Back to the reconciliation UI — here's the 'delta explanation' list. Each potential delta is given a confidence score. For instance tokenization mismatch is medium confidence, sampling extrapolation is high if you enabled a sampling flag, and reserved capacity amortization is very high where reservations are present.

[13:10] Liam: Can we set the attribution algorithm to not split infra but to bill direct to a shared team? We have a shared infra pool.
[13:16] Priya: Yep — you can create a grouping rule that assigns routes to a 'Shared-Infra' account and then allocate a single amortized line for the reservation. The rollups will then show team-level and shared infra lines separately.

[13:38] Sanjay: For audit, how long are logs retained? We need 1 year for some regs.
[13:44] Alex: Audit logs retention depends on plan. Hosted default is 90 days on the UI, with extended retention add-on for 12 months or longer. For Private deployments retention is under customer control.

[14:05] Nina: About anomalies — can console alert on sudden cost spikes per route?
[14:10] Priya: Yes. You can create alerting rules on percent change in daily spend, on token spikes, or on latency regressions. Alerts can go to Slack, PagerDuty, or email.

[14:35] Liam: For the pilot, would Redwood run collection in full-capture mode for 2 weeks and we compare with our billing exports?
[14:41] Alex: That's the plan we usually recommend. We'll set full capture for triage-bot and triage-embed for 2 weeks, share the export and run reconciliation with your FinOps.

[15:02] Priya: Quick note on optimization suggestions — the Console's Optimize tab will suggest quantization options, batching window changes, and model variant swaps with estimated cost delta and expected impact to latency. It will also show historical tests where similar changes had X% latency change in customer cases.

[15:28] Sanjay: If we adopt a recommended quantized model and it degrades output quality slightly, can we tie quality regressions to prompts/test set?
[15:35] Priya: Yes — we have eval hooks. You can upload a prompt-set and Redwood will run side-by-side comparisons and report scoring metrics. If quality regresses beyond a threshold we'll flag it in the rollout and can auto-fallback.

[15:58] Nina: Are there guardrails for canary rollouts? We don't want canaries to suddenly spin up too much compute.
[16:04] Priya: Canary policies let you cap request rate, cap token budget, and set automatic rollback criteria based on error or quality metrics. Also canaries can be routed to dedicated burst capacity so you don't hit shared pool limits.

[16:30] Alex: All right, let's talk deliverables. We'll put together a pilot config and the sample export. We'll also loop in Security for the SSO/KMS conversation.

[16:45] Liam: For success criteria — Sanjay wants within 3% reconciliation delta for the pilot and Nina wants rollups by product and team to be exportable to their ledger.
[16:55] Sanjay: If we can get under 3-5% unexplained delta that's acceptable for the first pass. We understand differences but want to be able to explain them.

[17:10] Priya: Noted. We'll enable full capture and a matching time-bucket to make the comparison apples-to-apples.

[17:25] Alex: Ok final demo note: the per-route dashboard includes an interactive 'explain this cost' button that surfaces the dominant drivers — tokens, model variant, infra amortization, KV hits. You can click into the request traces as well.

[18:00] (wrap-up) Alex: Recap of next steps — Alex will share the export template and pricing notes; Priya will do the triage-bot trial run and send latency/cost comparison; Security follow-up to be scheduled. Any final questions?
[18:15] Nina: One logistical question — what's the timeline to enable customer-managed KMS on Hosted?
[18:20] Alex: It's in beta Q2 2026; we'll add you to the early access list and include a data sheet.
[18:27] Liam: Cool. Also can you include an example ledger export?
[18:30] Alex: Yes — sample GL mapping will be included.
[18:35] Sanjay: Thanks all. Looking forward to the pilot.
[18:40] Priya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

[18:50] (end)

Notes: minor transcription errors present (route name sometimes transcribed as triaged-bot); occasional speaker overlap.
